children.label: Ideal IV agent
children: Rapid onset: lipid soluble and mostly un-ionized at blood pH
Rapid recovery through redistribution
Analgesia at sub-anesthetic doses
Minimal CVS and respiratory depression
No nausea, excitation, emergence phenomena or histamine release
No pain on injection, no venous sequelae, water soluble
Does not stimulate porphyria

children.label: Classification
children: Barbiturate: thiopental
Non-barbiturate: propofol, ketamine, etomidate
Adjuvants: benzodiazepines (midazolam, diazepam)

children.label: Thiopental
children: Ultra-short barbiturate, 3-5 mg/kg gives sleep in 30-60 s
Usual induction 3-6 mg/kg; very small doses in shock or frail elderly
Short action from redistribution to muscle and fat
Enhances GABA; lowers ICP and intraocular pressure
Myocardial depression, hypotension, apnea, laryngospasm
Contraindications: airway obstruction, porphyria, hypersensitivity
Caution: CVS, hepatic and renal disease
Intra-arterial injection: dilute with saline, heparinize, brachial plexus block

children.label: Propofol
children: Alkylphenol; 1% emulsion (soybean oil, glycerol, egg phosphatide)
Induction 2.5-3 mg/kg (1.5-2 premedicated, 1 or less elderly)
TIVA 50-150 mcg/kg/min; sedation 25-75 mcg/kg/min
No histamine release, no MH trigger, low PONV, antiemetic and anticonvulsant
Lowers cerebral blood flow and ICP
Hypotension more than thiopental and impaired baroreflex; profound respiratory depression
Pain on injection: add lidocaine or use a larger vein
Contraindications (slide): egg allergy, cannot maintain airway, fixed cardiac output, shock

children.label: Ketamine
children: Dissociative agent related to PCP, acts on NMDA receptors
IV 1-2 mg/kg, IM 5-10 mg/kg
Raises BP, heart rate, cardiac output, ICP and intraocular pressure
Bronchodilator, preserves airway reflexes, increases secretions
Unpleasant dreams, hallucinations, delirium
Uses: asthmatics, CV collapse needing emergency surgery, induction
Contraindications: psychosis, cerebrovascular disease, hypertension hazardous, raised ICP

children.label: Etomidate
children: Acts on GABA receptors, induction 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
Hemodynamically neutral, no analgesia
Adverse: nausea and vomiting, injection pain, myoclonus
Transient adrenal insufficiency: caution with chronic steroids

children.label: Benzodiazepines
children: Amnesia, anticonvulsant, minimal cardiorespiratory depression
Facilitate GABA; metabolized by liver conjugation
Midazolam: 2-3x more potent, faster onset, more amnesia, half-life 1-4 h
Diazepam: longer acting (21-37 h), more post-op sedation, more injection pain
Flumazenil: competitive antagonist, 0.2 mg over 15 s then 0.1 mg/min up to 2 mg
Flumazenil half-life about 1 h, so sedation may recur

children.label: Opioids
children: Opium alkaloids: morphine (strongest), codeine
Mu: analgesia, respiratory depression, euphoria, dependence
Kappa: analgesia, sedation, miosis; sigma: dysphoria
Fentanyl: opioid most used for induction, 100x morphine potency, about 30 min
Morphine: long analgesia, give under 5 mg/min (histamine release)
Effects: slow deep breathing, bradycardia, low SVR, constipation, biliary colic, urinary retention, chest wall rigidity
Naloxone reverses (onset 1-2 min, lasts 30-60 min); high doses cause abrupt pain, hypertension, pulmonary edema, arrest
